inputs.declared_question: How can a system make cross-perspective usefulness visible without treating agreement as truth or majority rule?

internal_region.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

source_facts.claim: Community Notes lets contributors collaboratively write and rate contextual notes, and its official documentation says visible notes require helpful ratings across differing perspectives rather than raw majority rule.
The system infers differing perspectives from prior note-rating patterns and does not use demographics, declared political affiliation, follows, or posts to decide a note's rating status.
The ranking documentation describes matrix factorization that produces one global note status rather than personalized note scores, with publicly inspectable source and evolving safeguards.
FN-14 explicitly names Community Notes as an open reference for ranking contributions that achieve helpfulness across differing perspectives.

cartographer.inference: Community Notes offers one inspectable technical organ for identifying contextual notes found helpful across differing rating perspectives. It can inform a Cyberdelic shared-reality practice, but it neither establishes truth nor preserves the full evidence, testimony, values, provenance, and dissent imagined by FN-25.
cartographer.uncertainty: Rating-derived perspective space can miss differences that are absent from the contributor pool or not expressed through past rating behavior. Community Notes also changes over time and operates inside one centrally governed platform.
cartographer.attribution: External factual descriptions are attributed to the official Community Notes Guide and the twitter/communitynotes public repository. Internal continuity is attributed to the exact FN-S0-001 publication.
cartographer.stop_reason: One external node and two deliberately different edges fully used the three-candidate budget. The Cartographer stopped without surveying other fact-checking or deliberation systems.

decisions.decision: Keep the Community Notes node strongly evidenced and the FN-14 adjacency strong because the exact field note explicitly names the project as an open technical reference.

Keep the FN-25 shared inquiry possible and emerging. Cross-perspective helpfulness is one signal, while a Cyberdelic storm may preserve several claim kinds, alternative branches, and unresolved dissent.
Rotate the finite Attending arrangement to FN-14 and Community Notes, archive the WebAssembly arrangement, and leave relationships.json unchanged because proposal publication is not ratification.

unresolved_questions: Which kinds of disagreement remain invisible when perspective is inferred only from rating patterns?
What does a public storm need beyond a note that people across perspectives find helpful?
How can broad helpfulness become one signal among evidence, testimony, values, provenance, and explicit dissent?
